“…She's seriously angry…”

I have no idea why.

No, I genuinely have no idea at all, but…

“Still, she…”

She seems completely different from the Tohsaka I know at school.

目の前にはずんずんと歩いていく学校のアイドル、憧れていた遠坂凛がいて、

Ahead of me marches the idol of our school, the girl I admired, Rin Tohsaka.

Behind me follows a silent blonde girl—Saber, who calls herself a Servant.

あ。
なんか、廊下が異次元空間のような気がしてきた。

pages.en:
“…………”

Ah.

The corridor is beginning to feel like some other dimension.

が、いつまでも腑抜けのままではいられない。
俺だって半人前と言えど魔術師だ。
同じく魔術師であるらしい遠坂がここまで堂々としているのだから、俺だってしっかりしなければ馬鹿にされる。

But I cannot remain stupefied forever.

Half-trained or not, I am a mage too.

If Tohsaka, apparently a mage herself, can carry herself with this much assurance, I have to pull myself together or she will think me a fool.

まず、後ろに付いてきているセイバー。
彼女が俺をマスターと呼び、契約したというからには使い魔の類であるのは間違いない。

…Though there is very little I can work out on my own.

First, there is Saber, following behind me.

She calls me Master and says we have formed a contract, so she must be some kind of familiar.

たいていは魔術師の体の一部を移植され、分身として使役されるモノを言うのだとか。
使い魔とは魔術師の助けとなるモノ。
故に、できるだけ魔術師に負担をかけないよう、あまり魔力を必要としない小動物が適任とされる。

I was taught that a familiar is a kind of assistant to a mage.

Most receive a transplanted piece of the mage's body and are employed as extensions of the mage himself.

A familiar exists to aid its mage.

Small animals are therefore considered ideal, since sustaining them requires little magical energy and places less strain on the mage.

pages.ja:
確かにそう教わりはしたけど、しかし。
「？ 何かあるのですか、シロウ」
「……ああいや、なんでもない」
pages.jaRuby:
確かにそう教わりはしたけど、しかし。
「？ 何かあるのですか、シロウ」
「……ああいや、なんでもない」
pages.en:
That is what I was taught. And yet—

“Is something the matter, Shirou?”

“…No. It's nothing.”

pages.ja:
……セイバーはどう見ても人間だ。しかも明らかに主である俺より優れている。
そんな相手を縛り付ける魔力なんて俺にはないし、そもそも使い魔を使役するだけの魔術回路もない。

pages.en:
…No matter how I look at her, Saber is human. Worse, she is plainly superior to me, her supposed Master.

I do not possess enough magical energy to bind someone like her, nor the Magic Circuits needed to command a familiar in the first place.

pages.ja:
「…………」
だから、きっとセイバーは使い魔とは似て非なるモノの筈だ。
彼女は自分をサーヴァントと言っていた。
それがどんなモノかは知らないが、あのランサーという男も、遠坂が連れていた赤い男も同じモノなのだと思う。

“……”

Saber must therefore be something similar to a familiar but fundamentally distinct from one.

She called herself a Servant.

I have no idea what that means, but the man called Lancer and the man in red who accompanied Tohsaka must have been the same kind of being.

pages.ja:
セイバーは遠坂もマスターと呼んでいた。
なら、サーヴァントを連れた魔術師をマスターと呼ぶのだろう。

pages.en:
Saber called Tohsaka a Master too.

Then perhaps any mage accompanied by a Servant is called a Master.

pages.ja:
……遠坂も魔術師らしいが、彼女が何者なのか俺には知る由もない。
衛宮家は切嗣の代からこの町にやって来たよそ者だ。
だから遠坂が魔術師だとは知らなかったし、遠坂の方も俺が魔術を習っている、なんて知らなかったに違いない。

…Tohsaka also appears to be a mage, but I have no means of knowing what she truly is.

The Emiya family are outsiders who came to this town in Kiritsugu's generation.

That is why I never knew Tohsaka was a mage—and Tohsaka surely never knew that I was studying magecraft.

……この町には、俺の知らない魔術師が複数いる。
ランサーとやらも他の魔術師の使い魔だとしたら、俺はつまり、魔術師同士の争いに足を突っ込んだという事だろうか

pages.en:
…There are several magi in this town whom I know nothing about.

If this Lancer is another mage's familiar, then I have somehow stumbled into a conflict between magi—

pages.ja:

なんて言いながら居間に入っていく遠坂。
「………………」
考えるのはここまでだ。
とにかく遠坂に話を聞く為に居間に入る。

pages.en:
“Oh, it's quite spacious. A Japanese-style house is a novelty too. Emiya, is that the living room?”

Tohsaka talks as she walks straight inside.

“………………”

That is enough speculation.

I follow her into the living room to hear what she has to say.

時計は午前一時を回っていた。

pages.en:
I turn on the lights.

It is past one in the morning.

pages.en:
“God, it's freezing! The window is completely shattered!”

“I couldn't help it. That guy Lancer attacked me. I didn't exactly have time to worry about the furniture.”

pages.en:
“Oh, that explains it. So you fought him alone until you managed to summon Saber?”

“I didn't fight him. He beat me without my landing a blow.”

pages.en:
“Hmm. You don't even pretend otherwise. …I see, I see. You really are exactly what you look like, Emiya.”

For some reason, that pleases her. Tohsaka walks over to the broken window.

the shattered pieces of the window fit themselves back together, restoring the pane in a matter of seconds.

Tohsaka speaks as though it were nothing.

Needless to say, her skill lies wholly beyond my comprehension.

“What? Of course you can. Working with glass is the most elementary of basics.

“Repairing glass that broke only a few minutes ago is practically an entrance examination in any school of magecraft.”

“—What?”

Tohsaka stops dead.

…Damn. I seem to have said something I should not have.

…Well, I use the shed for training. But if I called *that* a workshop, Tohsaka might become genuinely furious.

おう、と素直に頷いた。

“………I doubt it, but I need to make sure. You do know how to handle the Five Great Elements and establish a path, don't you?”

I nod frankly. That's right. I don't.

うわ、こわっ。
なまじ美人なだけに黙り込むともの凄く迫力あるぞ、こいつ。

pages.en:
“………………”

Whoa. Terrifying.

She's beautiful to begin with, so when she falls silent like this, the sheer force of her presence is incredible.

「そんな事ないぞ。一応、強化の魔術ぐらいは使える」
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“What, then? You're a complete amateur?”

“Of course not. I can use Reinforcement, at least.”

さすがに視線が痛くて、なんとも煮え切らない返答をしてしまった。

“Reinforcement… Of all the half-baked disciplines to practice. And you're hopeless at everything else?”

“…Well, put plainly, probably.”

Her stare is so painful that the answer comes out hopelessly evasive.

pages.en:

“…………Hmph.”

That irritates me.

It is not as though I have been playing around.

My inexperience may be a fact, but that has nothing to do with this.

pages.en:
“Well, never mind. Complaining about what's already decided won't accomplish anything. More importantly, I have a debt to repay.”

Tohsaka exhales and collects herself.

こくん、と頷く。

“Then let's begin.

“Emiya, you have no idea what position you're in, do you?”

I nod.

“?”

That turn of phrase sounded strange, but interrupting her here might get me punched, so I hold my tongue.

pages.en:
“To put it plainly, Emiya, you have been chosen as a Master.

“There should be a sacred mark somewhere on one of your hands. The location differs from person to person—it might be on the back of your hand or on your arm—but it should take the form of three Command Spells. Those are proof that you are a Master.”

“The back of my hand… Oh, you mean these.”

pages.ja:
「そ。それはサーヴァントを律する呪文でもあるから大切にね。令呪っていうんだけど、それがある限りはサーヴァントを従えていられるわ」
「……？ ある限りって、どういう事だよ」

pages.en:
“Exactly. They're also the curses by which you control your Servant, so take good care of them. They're called Command Spells, and as long as you possess them, you can keep your Servant under control.”

“…? What do you mean, ‘as long as’?”

で、その令呪がなくなったら衛宮くんは殺されるだろうから、せいぜい注意して」

“Command Spells grant absolute authority. Each mark is a curse capable of overriding your Servant's will and compelling absolute obedience.

“You don't need an incantation to activate one. The thought that you mean to use it is enough.

“And once your Command Spells are gone, you'll probably be killed, Emiya, so do be careful.”

pages.en:
“What—?”

Wait. Wait a minute.

I cannot understand a word Tohsaka is saying.

Masters defeat other Masters.

And in the end someone wins the Holy Grail… The Holy Grail? Does she mean *that* Holy Grail…!?

“You still don't understand? In simple terms, you've been drawn into a game.

“The Holy Grail War—a struggle for survival among seven Masters. A contest to the death between magi that cannot end until every other Master has been defeated.”

Rin Tohsaka states it as though it were nothing at all.

“—”

The words I just heard turn endlessly through my head.

I have been chosen as a Master.

Tohsaka is a Master too.

Servants are familiars.

—And then there is

the Holy Grail War, a fight to the death against other magi—

“I understand how you feel, but all I can do is tell you the facts.

“…And surely part of you already understands. Servants have tried to kill you not once, but twice. You must know there is no longer any way for you to escape.”

“——”

He did not nearly kill me. He killed me.

…That's right.

The man with the spear killed me.

Before I marvel at everything happening now, I ought to be marveling that I am alive at all.

pages.en:
…The wound punched through my chest.

…The blood draining away.

…The warmth fading from my body.

And then—

at the brink, the voice of someone who accepted what had happened with astonishing grace—

“Has it sunk in? You crossed that line long ago.

“Being ignorant won't let you run away. And if you're a mage, surely you're prepared for this much—for the fact that ours is a life of killing and being killed.”

Perhaps she enjoys seeing me bewildered. Tohsaka is in an excellent mood.

“The Masters wield their Servants as their own hands and feet to eliminate the others.

“—Those are the rules of the ritual called the Holy Grail War.”

She has listened to my conversation with Tohsaka in silence.

…She truly looks human in every respect.

I do not know what she is, but she is a girl who seems not much different from me in age.

“What? Heroes from the past, given flesh?”

“Exactly. Whether from antiquity or the modern age, a legendary hero who has died is drawn into this time and materialized.”
